text:
Alisa: Quick sync — we need to pick a home for ingress safety checks: edge proxies (eg nginx/sidecar) or central admission service? tradeoffs + final call by EOD.

Michael: Edge = lowest tail latency but harder to update policies + duplication across regions. Central = single source of truth, easier rollout but adds a hop and potential SLO risk.

Raj: Also think about abuse signals. Edge has access to raw traffic features for heuristics (IP, TLS SNI, header entropy). Central only gets structured request metadata unless we forward more.

Sara: Agreed. For quota accounting we already use central token bank. But admission decision could be hybrid: fast local checks + central for heavy decisions.

Alisa: Hybrid sounds promising. Can we define a minimal contract for edge->central when edge needs help? e.g., admission proto returns admit/queue/penalty and optionally fallthrough token.

Michael: Sketch API:
```
POST /v1/admit
{ client_id, session_id, features: {prefix_hash, rate_hint, abuse_score}}
=> {decision: "ADMIT" | "SOFT_SHED" | "REJECT", penalty_ms?: number, fallback_policy?: "proxy"}
```
Edge uses local rules first. If uncertain, call central with condensed features.

Raj: Two practical concerns: 1) cardinality of features — keep small to avoid high bandwidth. 2) privacy for Private deploys — features must be configurable.

Sara: For throughput, central must be able to answer O(10k) qps per region in worst case. We'll need async caching: edge caches recent admits keyed by (client_id, prefix_hash, policy_version).

Alisa: Okay. What about abuse-score propagation and staleness? If central marks a client as abusive, edges should converge quickly.

Michael: Use two-phase signals: immediate short-live flag (ttl ~30s) pushed via pub/sub for hot clients + longer-lived reputation in central DB. Edge consumes push updates to invalidate caches.

Raj: When central is unreachable, edges should implement deterministic fallback: token-bucket local admission with conservative weights and emit telemetry (so central can reconcile later).

Sara: Also we need a safety circuit: if central latency > X ms or error rate > Y%, edges switch to degraded mode and log counts. ops-bot should alert when degraded for >2m.

ops-bot: :warning: Alert rule suggested: central_admit_5m_error_rate > 1% OR central_p95_latency > 200ms -> Pager to oncall. (config link: https://go/redwood/rules/ingress-admit)

Alisa: Nice. Let's capture interface versioning: include policy_version in responses. Edges must send policy_version header with requests; central rejects mismatched versions with code 409 and provide new version metadata.

Michael: Rollout plan: 1) implement central API + fake edge caller in staging; 2) add push invalidation; 3) enable hybrid in canary region with conservative soft-shed thresholds; 4) monitor key metrics (admit rate, p99 latency, token divergence).

Raj: Telemetry: emit admit_decision, feature_hash, policy_version, fallback_used, and central_latency. Keep sample rate low for high-traffic clients but full for errors.

Alisa: Decision summary: hybrid admission. Edges run cheap deterministic checks, call central for ambiguous cases. Push-based invalidation for abuse flags. Deterministic fallback token-bucket when central missing. Ops alerting for central degraded state.

Sara: I'll write the RFC follow-up with API proto, cache key shapes, and rollout checklist. Will ping owners for infra + runtime.

Michael: I'll prototype the admit service handler and a simulated edge harness.

Raj: I'll design the abuse propagation format and privacy knobs for Private deployments.

Alisa: Great — target RFC PR by Thursday. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
